title: From “Materials Historian” to “Technological Innovator”—Industrial Archaeology as an Indispensable Prerequisite for Creative Technological Innovation
content: Technological innovation is a highly relevant, yet multifaceted, topic. What type of technological innovation is best suited to the profile of a materials scientist? What specific interests are required of this kind of technological innovator, and what skills or training must they possess? While creativity is undoubtedly an essential requirement, knowledge of past scientific achievements serves as another cornerstone for this type of activity. “Scientific” technological innovation is closely related to invention; it relies on a creative spark—in this case, one applied to the findings of the past. This brief note uses an example from the field of nanotechnology to illustrate how technological innovation is implemented and how it plays a role in refining and completing scientific discoveries, ultimately elevating them to an industrial Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
